I am an old woman now, 63 years, and my back does not bend like before. This land of mine, about one and a bit hectares, I have worked it many seasons with maize, and I plant pigeon peas and pumpkins between the rows so the soil stays strong and we have relish. I will try to get some fertilizer from the subsidy coupon if they give me one — the maize does not grow well here in Salima without it, the soil is tired. I keep a few chickens and I sweep the kraal for manure to add in the planting holes. For seed, my neighbor and the extension man say the hybrid SC403 is good, so if I have money after buying salt and soap I will buy a small packet, but I may also plant some of my own kept seed. The army worms came last year and ate my young maize badly, so if I see them again I will buy a small sachet of chemical from the trading centre. I cannot carry water to the field — I depend on the rains, may God send them well. My daughter-in-law helps me weed, and I will call piecework people for one or two days when the weeds are too much for me.
